evaluation.positioning_hook: After her cousin is killed by police, a grieving Dallas woman leads a zoo break-in for justice — and gets trapped in a night of escaped predators, betrayal, and viral fallout.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The hook is immediate and legible: grief, revenge, a zoo break-in, and animal chaos give it a clean commercial engine. The audience is real and sizable, but the racial-politics framing and hard violence narrow it from four-quadrant to a more adult genre lane.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The premise lands fast in the opening pages: Dre is killed, James is radicalized, and the zoo heist begins. The script keeps the central engine clear even as it escalates into a survival thriller.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: James has a strong emotional spine, and Chidi/Abasi gives the story a genuinely slippery counterforce. Terrell, Brett, and Madyline each add pressure, though the ensemble is more functional than deeply iconic.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The combination of protest rage, zoo infiltration, and predator-set-piece survival is unusual and confident. The script also takes a bold late turn into manipulation and identity fraud, which gives the material a sharper edge than a standard creature feature.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: Once the break-in starts, the script is relentlessly forward-driving: security room, tiger, roof, tram, tunnel, sanctuary, and final escape all escalate cleanly. The set pieces are built to keep the reader leaning in.

resonant_originality.reasoning: It feels fresh because the revenge premise is not just emotional but spatially specific: a zoo full of dangerous animals becomes the pressure cooker. The final reveal recontextualizing Chidi/Abasi adds a second layer of surprise that feels baked into the premise rather than tacked on.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The zoo is rendered as a functioning ecosystem with staff, transport tunnels, vet stations, exhibits, and security protocols that generate story. The outside world — protests, curfew, media frenzy — also gives the story a broader social frame.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The script has a distinct register: street-level anger, darkly comic banter, and creature-feature panic all coexist without feeling random. The tonal identity is strongest when the script lets grief and absurdity sit side by side.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: The James/Dre wound, the racialized public response, and the final manipulation reveal suggest more beneath the surface than a simple escape thriller. The story is still primarily a one-night pressure cooker, but it carries enough thematic residue to linger.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: James and Chidi/Abasi create a strong push-pull dynamic, while Terrell, Brett, and Madyline keep the group volatile. The relationships generate conflict well, though the ensemble is more survival-functional than richly recursive.

lead_characters.name: James McKenzie
lead_characters.hook: James is Dre’s cousin and the emotional center of the film: guarded, furious, and carrying the kind of grief that can curdle into purpose. She reads as the least performative person in the room, which makes her both the most credible leader and the most vulnerable to being manipulated by someone who understands her pain.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Jurnee Smollett in Lovecraft Country or Letitia Wright in Mangrove — a role that demands controlled rage, moral fracture, and a final emotional reckoning. It gives an actor the chance to play leadership, guilt, and physical survival in the same breath.

lead_characters.name: Chidi Obasanjo
lead_characters.hook: Presented as a nervous zoo employee with a family on the line, Chidi is the story’s most consequential deception: a man who appears gentle, useful, and morally adjacent to James’ cause, then reveals a far darker agenda. The role is built on withheld identity, quiet authority, and the ability to pivot from ally to predator without losing plausibility.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Daniel Kaluuya in Judas and the Black Messiah or Walton Goggins in The Hateful Eight — a role where stillness, charm, and menace all have to coexist. It gives an actor a late-reveal transformation and a chance to reframe every earlier scene.

lead_characters.name: Terrell
lead_characters.hook: Terrell is the volatile pressure valve in the group: funny, defensive, impulsive, and increasingly dangerous as the night goes on. He’s the kind of character who can pivot from comic relief to liability to outright threat, which keeps every scene with him unstable.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Lakeith Stanfield in Short Term 12 or Michael K. Williams in The Wire — a role that lets an actor weaponize charisma and then turn it into danger. The appeal is the volatility: every beat can flip the room.

lead_characters.name: Brett
lead_characters.hook: Brett is James’ boyfriend and the story’s most visible bridge between worlds: well-meaning, emotionally sincere, and ultimately out of his depth. He’s useful because he’s not a villain, which makes his fear, guilt, and final sacrifice land harder.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Lucas Hedges in Manchester by the Sea or Paul Mescal in Aftersun — a role built on tenderness, helplessness, and the ache of not being enough. It gives an actor a chance to play love under pressure without turning him into a stock boyfriend.

lead_characters.name: Madyline
lead_characters.hook: Madyline is the most emotionally exposed member of the crew, and the one most likely to say the thing everyone else is avoiding. Her guilt, jealousy, and fear make her a live wire, and the script uses her to surface the private damage inside the mission.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Auli'i Cravalho in The Power or Jessie Buckley in Wild Rose — a role that lets an actor play insecurity, longing, and panic with real volatility. The late-film trauma turn gives the part a brutal physical and emotional payoff.

lead_characters.name: Corbett
lead_characters.hook: Corbett is the hard-edged DART operator who gives the zoo’s security apparatus a face and a pulse. He’s not overwritten, but he’s effective as a professional predator whose calm makes the eventual chaos feel more dangerous.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Josh Brolin in Sicario or Stephen Lang in Avatar — a role for an actor who can project authority, fatigue, and lethal competence in a few scenes. It’s a clean, efficient antagonist-supporting turn.

lead_characters.name: Dr. Miranda Sands
lead_characters.hook: Dr. Sands is the vet who understands the animals better than the people around her, which makes her one of the story’s few grounded moral presences. She’s practical, compassionate, and trapped inside a system that’s already slipping out of control.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Laura Linney in The Big C or Carrie Coon in The Leftovers — a role that lets an actor play competence under siege and empathy under pressure. It’s a strong supporting part for someone who can make authority feel humane.

lead_characters.name: Zoo Director
lead_characters.hook: The Zoo Director is a bureaucratic coward with just enough authority to make everyone else’s night worse. He’s a useful pressure character because he embodies institutional panic without needing a full arc.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of J.K. Simmons in Whiplash or Richard Jenkins in The Visitor — a role that lets an actor play brittle authority and self-preservation. It’s a compact, memorable supporting turn.

lead_characters.name: Frey
lead_characters.hook: Frey is the bored security tech whose casual indifference becomes the hinge for the break-in going bad. He’s not a big character, but he’s the kind of small role that can snap the plot into a new gear.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Jesse Plemons in a small but pivotal role — a part that lives on deadpan realism and sudden panic. It gives an actor a sharp, scene-stealing beat.

lead_characters.name: Real Chidi
lead_characters.hook: The real Chidi is the story’s hidden moral inversion: the man James thinks is a desperate helper is actually the legitimate zoo employee whose identity has been hijacked. He functions less as a conventional character than as the key to the film’s final reframe.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of a late-reveal role in a prestige thriller, where the actor gets to recontextualize the entire story in a single scene. It’s a strong twist-part for someone who can play credibility and betrayal at once.

casting_characteristics: One lead role with heavy emotional and physical demands
Several 20s-40s supporting roles with strong dialect/voice specificity
Animal-performance coordination required for multiple scenes

notable_requirements: Dallas zoo environment with tunnels, exhibits, vet station, security room, tram, and sanctuary areas
Night exterior work across a large controlled campus
Practical animal enclosures and controlled stunt-safe pathways

technical.vfx_details: Animal escalation, crowd/protest inserts, and some environmental enhancement for chaos and containment; most major beats appear designed for practical staging with selective augmentation.
technical.sfx_needs: Blood effects, animal attack simulation, breakaway glass, smoke/siren/environmental chaos, and practical rigging for tram/cablecar sequences.

platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release; best suited to streaming-first or specialty theatrical genre rollout

budget.note: A large zoo campus, multiple night exteriors, animal attack sequences, tram/cablecar work, and a finale with broad chaos push this above a simple contained-thriller footprint, though it still looks scope-manageable with disciplined production design.

casting.note: James needs an actor who can carry grief, leadership, and physical survival; Terrell and Chidi/Abasi each need sharply calibrated turns that can pivot from ally to threat. The ensemble is castable, but the lead and twist-support roles are the key lifts.

development.note: The late identity reveal around Chidi/Abasi is the script’s biggest structural swing, and the film also asks the audience to track a lot of animal-set-piece geography. The concept is clear, but the final act depends on the manipulation reveal landing cleanly.

comp_set.title: Crawl
comp_set.why_it_comps: A contained survival thriller that turns a specific animal environment into a relentless pressure cooker.

comp_set.title: Nope
comp_set.why_it_comps: A genre film that uses spectacle, animals, and social unease to create a bigger cultural conversation around the set pieces.

comp_set.title: Green Room
comp_set.why_it_comps: A trapped-group escalation model where every new room and decision makes the situation more dangerous.

comp_set.title: The Invitation
comp_set.why_it_comps: The slow reveal of hidden motives and the way social trust collapses into survival mode.

audience_target.primary_audience: Adults who like elevated survival thrillers with social bite, especially viewers drawn to tense, violent, high-concept genre films.
audience_target.demographics: 18-44 skew, slightly male-leaning but with strong female appeal; urban and streaming-native genre audience; culturally engaged viewers who respond to race, justice, and media-satire subtext.

budget_tier.note: A contemporary zoo setting, limited principal cast, and mostly night exteriors keep it in indie feature territory, though the animal work and tram/cablecar sequences require disciplined scope control.

types_of_buyers: producer-directors looking for a breakout contained feature
buyers building socially charged adult genre slates
lane_fit.detail: This sits naturally in the lane of adult, concept-forward genre with a social edge: a contained survival movie that can sell on premise, then deepen on performance and theme. The zoo setting gives it a clean marketing image, while the racial and media-frenzy backdrop gives it conversation value.

ip_potential.detail: Standalone feature with a closed survival arc and a twist ending that resolves the central manipulation; no clear sequel or spinoff vector emerges from the page.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The zoo is a great pressure-cooker setting.
strengths.what_it_means: The setting gives the movie a built-in marketing image and a production-friendly arena where every enclosure can become a new set piece. Buyers can see the trailer in their heads: one night, one campus, escalating animal danger.
strengths.evidence: The script moves from security room to tunnels to gift shop roof to polar bear enclosure to tram to sanctuary, each space changing the rules.

strengths.dimension_or_area: James has a strong emotional engine.
strengths.what_it_means: A grieving lead with a clear wound and a dangerous sense of purpose is exactly the kind of role that can attract a serious young actress and anchor word-of-mouth. The part gives the film a human center so the animal chaos never feels empty.
strengths.evidence: Her guilt over Dre, her lie to Chidi about the money, and her final choice to keep going after multiple deaths all sharpen her arc.

strengths.what_it_means: Each major sequence adds a new survival problem rather than repeating the last one, which is what keeps a contained thriller feeling expensive on the page. That makes the script easier to pitch as a momentum movie rather than a concept-only movie.
strengths.evidence: Tiger attack, roof crossing, polar bear encounter, mandrill assault, alligator sanctuary, and final cart chase all introduce distinct threats.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The social context gives it bite.
strengths.what_it_means: The opening police shooting and the viral/public-response material give the film a topical edge that can widen the conversation beyond genre fans. That helps position it for buyers looking for elevated genre with cultural relevance.
strengths.evidence: The livestream of Dre’s death, the protests, the curfew, and the media montage at the end all frame the story as more than a creature feature.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The Chidi reveal adds a second engine.
strengths.what_it_means: The late identity reversal turns the movie from a straightforward escape thriller into a manipulation thriller, which increases rewatch value and gives the ending a sharper sting. It also creates a strong talking point for marketing and post-screening discussion.
strengths.evidence: The interrogation-room reveal that Chidi is really Abasi, plus the final cargo-ship button, reframes the entire mission.

whats_special.headline: This is a clean, high-concept survival thriller with a strong lead role, a memorable setting, and a set-piece ladder that keeps climbing. It also has the kind of social edge and twist-reveal packaging that can help a buyer justify a genre buy to both marketing and development.

items.area: The Chidi/Abasi reveal is the biggest buy-risk.
items.detail: The script asks the audience to accept a major identity fraud after spending most of the film treating Chidi as a sympathetic helper. That late reframe is juicy, but it is also the point where the movie either feels cleverly recontextualized or like it has withheld too much for too long.

items.area: The animal escalation pushes the VFX/stunt load.
items.detail: Tiger, polar bear, mandrill, hippo, alligators, snakes, and multiple enclosure interactions create a lot of creature-specific execution pressure. Even if much of it is practical, the number of distinct animal beats will be the first budget conversation after the premise conversation.

items.area: The ensemble is functional, not deeply modular.
items.detail: James carries the movie, and the supporting players mostly exist to pressure her or die around her. That works for a feature, but it means the script’s relationship engine is narrower than the scale of the chaos suggests.

items.area: The opening protest material narrows the lane.
items.detail: The police shooting, viral outrage, and media commentary give the film urgency, but they also make the movie more politically charged than a standard creature thriller. That is a strength for some buyers and a filter for others.

items.area: The zoo geography is dense enough to track carefully.
items.detail: The tunnels, exhibits, tram, sanctuary, vet station, and rooftop crossings all work individually, but the film asks the audience to keep a lot of spatial information in play while the action is moving fast. That is manageable, but it is a real clarity dependency in the back half.

issues.headline: The script’s main friction point is the late Chidi/Abasi reveal: it’s the most original move in the piece, but also the one most likely to split readers on first pass. Beyond that, the project is a real production lift because the zoo action keeps widening into new animal and location demands even as the story stays contained.
